interpretation: Above 1.0 means work cost less than the budget for it
caveats: Unreliable before about 15 to 20 percent complete

interpretation: Above 1.0 means more work is in place than planned
caveats: Cost-weighted, so it is not a measure of the critical path

interpretation: Positive is favourable
caveats: Same early-project caveat as CPI

interpretation: Positive is ahead of plan
caveats: A positive SV with a late critical path is common and misleading

interpretation: Projects the overrun if the current cost efficiency persists
caveats: Assumes the current efficiency continues, which is a judgement

interpretation: The most defensible forecast where the cost to complete is maintained
caveats: Only as good as the cost to complete behind it

inputs: Actual cost, budget at completion, earned value
interpretation: Projects no repeat of past variance
caveats: Rarely true in practice; use for one-off disruption only

interpretation: Remaining cost to finish
caveats: Define whether commitments are included to avoid double counting

inputs: Budget at completion, estimate at completion
interpretation: Negative means forecast overrun
caveats: Restate BAC if the budget was revised without a change order

interpretation: The efficiency needed to finish on budget; above 1.0 means harder than achieved so far
caveats: Above about 1.1 the recovery is usually not credible

interpretation: Cost consumed against forecast final cost
caveats: Can look flattering when recorded cost lags field progress

interpretation: Physical progress by measured quantities
caveats: Needs a consistent unit and current quantities to mean anything

interpretation: Value of work performed to date under the contract
caveats: Commonly disputed with subcontractors; agree the measurement method

interpretation: Positive is overbilled, negative is underbilled
caveats: The core of the work in progress report and a cash-flow signal

interpretation: Forecast margin on the job
caveats: Excludes unapproved change orders unless you decide to include them

inputs: Budgeted hours to date, actual hours
interpretation: Above 1.0 means fewer hours than budgeted for the work installed
caveats: Only valid if hours are coded to the same cost codes as the estimate

interpretation: How much of the budget is spent regardless of progress
caveats: Read with percent complete; the gap between the two is the warning

formula: remaining revenue on awarded unperformed work
interpretation: Work under contract that has not yet been performed
caveats: Depends on a disciplined definition of 'awarded'

interpretation: Average collection period
caveats: Distorted by retentions and by a few large late payers

formula: retention percent x billings to date
interpretation: Cash held back until release milestones
caveats: Check the release conditions in the subcontract, not just the rate

formula: peak month outflows - peak month inflows
interpretation: The shallowest point in the cash forecast
caveats: Driven by billing cycle and pay-when-paid chains, not only by job performance

interpretation: Negative is ahead, positive is late
caveats: Only meaningful against an unedited baseline

formula: baseline total float - current total float
interpretation: How much contingency the plan has already used up
caveats: A leading indicator, and easy to obscure with logic changes

interpretation: The portion of the forecast not yet committed or spent
caveats: Define consistently with accounting to avoid double counting commitments
